title: How the Python SDK turns ZDX arguments into query parameters and bodies

prose.text: Most Python ZDX list and report methods carry the `zdx_params` decorator, which renames a few shorthand arguments to the API's query names before the request executor applies its own key conversion. The methods and their endpoints are generated (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface zdx`).

prose.label: Query names on the wire.
prose.text: {{params-conversion}} {{filter-names-camel-cased}} The user-ID filter's name differs across all three sources {{divergence:user-ids-param}}. Whether the API accepts the camel-cased names is open {{gap:camel-params-accepted}}.

prose.label: Methods without time ranges, and inventory.
prose.text: {{no-query-methods}} {{inventory-decorated}} Whether the inventory endpoint honors a time range is open {{gap:inventory-time-range}}. {{software-key}}

checks.do: Which client the Python program uses: on the OneAPI client, multiword filter names the decorator does not rename go out camel-cased.
Whether a filter was passed under a shorthand the decorator renames (`location_id`, `department_id`, `geo_id`, `search`, `since`) or under a name it leaves alone.

decorator-mapping.statement: `zdx_params` turns `since` into `from` and `to`, `search` into `q`, `location_id` into `loc`, `department_id` into `dept` and `geo_id` into `geo`, and passes `exclude_dept`, `exclude_loc`, `exclude_geo`, `score_bucket`, `limit`, `offset` and `expiry` under their own names, whether they come as keyword arguments or inside `query_params`.

quotes: # Then, process shorthand parameters if provided within query_params itself.

since-to-epoch.statement: A `since` value is a number of hours: the decorator sets `to` to the current Unix time and `from` to that time minus the hours times 3,600, unless the caller already set `from` or `to`.

score-bucket-check.statement: The `zdx_params` decorator rejects a `score_bucket` other than `poor`, `okay` or `good` with a ValueError before it calls the decorated method.

quotes: raise ValueError("Invalid value for score_bucket. Supported values: 'poor', 'okay', 'good'.")

params-conversion.statement: The request executor passes ZDX query parameters unchanged on the legacy ZDX client; otherwise, for any non-ZPA service, it runs every parameter name through `convert_keys_to_camel_case`, which maps each key with `to_lower_camel_case`: a name in `FIELD_EXCEPTIONS` takes its mapped value, any other name with an underscore is split on underscores, its first part lowercased and each later part capitalized.

quotes: else: # Normal param conversion if not ZPA
if string in FIELD_EXCEPTIONS: return FIELD_EXCEPTIONS[string]
if not string or "_" not in string: return string

filter-names-camel-cased.statement: So on the OneAPI client, multiword ZDX filter names that the decorator does not rename, such as `exclude_loc`, `exclude_dept`, `exclude_geo`, `score_bucket`, `user_ids`, `mac_address`, `private_ipv4` and `parent_geo_id`, reach the API camel-cased, while the contract names these parameters in snake_case (`exclude_loc`, `score_bucket`, `private_ipv4`, `mac_address`, `parent_geo_id`, and `userids` for user IDs).
filter-names-camel-cased.conditions: Follows from the executor's conversion and the helper's camel-casing rule; none of these names is in the helper's exceptions map at the pin. No captured request shows the wire names.

no-query-methods.statement: The Python deep-trace list takes only the device ID, and the deep-trace get and metric readers (`get_deeptrace`, `get_deeptrace_webprobe_metrics`, `get_deeptrace_cloudpath_metrics`, `get_deeptrace_cloudpath`, `get_deeptrace_health_metrics`, `get_deeptrace_events`) only the device and trace IDs; none takes query parameters, so they accept no time range.

inventory-decorated.statement: The Python `list_softwares` carries `zdx_params`, so a `since` passed to it is sent as `from` and `to`, although the contract lists no time-range parameters for the software inventory endpoint.

quotes:
@zdx_params
    def list_softwares(self, query_params: Optional[dict] = None) -> APIResult[List[DeviceSoftwareInventory]]:

inventory-decorated.conditions: The contract's parameter list for the endpoint at the pin is `loc`, `dept`, `geo`, `userids`, `deviceids`, `offset` and `limit`; a list cannot be pinned by pointer as complete, so the absence of `from` and `to` rests on that reading.

software-key.statement: The software-key read lists all users and devices for a given software name and version, and the Python SDK's example passes a key such as `screencaptureui2` to `list_software_keys`.

expect.description: The endpoint allows you to view the list of all users and devices for a given software name and version.

user-ids-param.summary: The device list's user-ID filter: the contract and the Go SDK call it `userids`; the Python SDK documents `user_ids`, which the decorator does not rename.

positions.says: The Python SDK takes `user_ids`, sent as written on the legacy client and camel-cased on the OneAPI client.

user-ids-param.impact: A Python device list filtered by user ID may come back unfiltered or rejected, because neither form it sends is the contract's name.

camel-params-accepted.title: Whether the ZDX API honors camel-cased or underscored query names it does not define
camel-params-accepted.detail: The Python OneAPI client camel-cases multiword ZDX filter names, and documents `user_ids` where the contract has `userids`. Whether the gateway or the ZDX API matches these names leniently, ignores them (returning unfiltered data) or rejects the request is not stated by any source.
camel-params-accepted.blocks: trusting Python ZDX queries that use exclusion, score-bucket, user, MAC, IP or parent-geolocation filters

inventory-time-range.title: Whether the software inventory endpoint honors a time range
inventory-time-range.detail: The Python `list_softwares` attaches `from` and `to` when given `since`; the contract lists no time-range parameters for the endpoint, which suggests the server ignores them, but no captured response confirms it.
inventory-time-range.blocks: answering whether an inventory listing reflects a time window
